newsitem.title: FINLAND: Ireland improving mining prospects - miner.
newsitem.headline: Ireland improving mining prospects - miner.

text.p: Ireland, home to Europe's largest zinc mine, is actively working with the mining industry to unravel bureaucracy and improve the country's investment climate, a mining executive told the Metal Bulletin base metals concentrates conference.

"Over the past five years, the industry and the government have worked together to ensure an attractive environment for future investment," said Tony O'Reilly, chief executive of Arcon International Resources Plc a junior exploration company which owns the Galmoy zinc operation.
The government is aware of mining requirements and is streamlining the process of obtaining planning and environmental permits, he said.
The government's position on corporate tax is also promising with the aim to reduce corporation tax to 10 percent by 2005 from 36 percent.
Meanwhile exploration is booming, with 428 prospecting licences granted.

The Galmoy mine development started production last year, a decade after its discovery, becoming the second operating zinc mine in Ireland. Arcon plans to build up annual production to 140,000 tonnes of zinc concentrate and 10,000 tonnes of lead concentrate, O'Reilly said.

The exploration programme at Galmoy has delineated additional resources of 2.2 million tonnes, grading 14.8 percent zinc and 2.15 percent lead, which increases Galmoy's mine life to more than 13 years, he said.
The biggest mine in Ireland -- and in Europe -- is Outokumpu's Tara mine, which together with the Galmoy mine will produce 430,000 tonnes of zinc concentrate next year.
The Tara mine last year produced 292,000 tonnes of zinc concentrate and 67,000 tonnes of lead concentrates.
Lisheen, a mining joint venture between Minorco and Ivernia West was granted planning permission earlier this month and is holding talks on obtaining a state mining lease.

Once all permits are obtained, possibly as soon as the third quarter this year the mine will undergo a two-year construction. It is expected to produce up to 300,000 tonnes of zinc concentrate and 40,000 tonnes of lead concentrate once it starts production in 2000, he added.
Also on the horizon, the Bula 8.5 million tonne orebody looks to be nearing the end of a 15-year legal battle, which could open it up to development.
